title: lore agent context auto-pins the bundle's Constitution into every profile's pack (OPAG-425 R8, LCLI-597 AC3 option B)
description: Ruled by opum-agent 2026-09-26T22:00:21Z (recorded in opum-doc Constitution/Constants ADR Amendment 4, f3f12e7). LCLI-597 AC3 said "lore init default .lore/agents profiles pin the Constitution", but lore init writes no agent profiles: nothing in src/ writes .lore/agents, and a default pin would fail lore check on a fresh init that has no Constitution. Option B was ruled instead: when the bundle has a Constitution (built-in type, not a profile-declared one, per R12), lore agent context adds it to every profile pack as a pinned source. When there is none it pins nothing and errors nothing. No new lore init output and no default profiles. Pack contents change additively; note that in the CHANGELOG.

acceptanceCriteria.text: With a built-in Constitution present, lore agent context <profile> for every profile carries it as a pinned source; with none present, packs are byte-identical to today, proven by tests including a positive control
A profile-declared Constitution (R12) is not auto-pinned, and an explicit pin of the same document is not duplicated
CHANGELOG notes the additive pack change; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: DESIGN (LCLI-609, branch feat/LCLI-609-autopin-constitution, cut from origin/dev e67b07af). Discovery: readAgentGovernance's walk was split into an exported discoverAgentGovernanceDocs(root) (src/commands/agent-governance.ts); readAgentGovernance is now agentBlockLines(discoverAgentGovernanceDocs(root)), so lore agents and lore agent context share ONE definition of the bundle's Constitution and R12 comes for free (typeRuleFor only yields a rule for lore's own built-in declaration). No second walk was written. Core: compilePack takes an optional constitutionPath; constitutionAutoPin resolves it to the loaded concept by path (fails loud, exit 6, if discovery found it on disk but the bundle did not load it) and returns a whole-document reference. ORDER: FIRST among pinned sources and first in the catalog, because it governs everything after it. PROVENANCE: catalog reason 'constitution' (a new value of the existing reason union; additive under cli-contract 7.1, same precedent as LCLI-432's missing-in-member/member-skipped); the profile's own pins keep reason 'pinned'. DEDUPE: no auto-pin when the profile references the Constitution's concept anywhere, pinned or sources, whole or by heading. That is the profile's own overlap rule (a whole-document reference overlaps every other reference to the same concept) applied to the auto-pin; it also gives an oversized Constitution an escape hatch. BUDGET: matches the existing over-budget pin behaviour exactly. The auto-pin is mandatory evidence, never truncated, and counted in the pinnedOnly floor. Over budget it exits 6 validation with the unchanged message; the hint gains a clause naming the Constitution and input gains constitution: <path>. Both are unchanged when there is no Constitution. SCOPE: every bare profile pack; the unknown-profile degraded pack (it has a Pinned evidence section, so it IS auto-pinned, and its warning and placeholder description then say 'and the auto-pinned Constitution'); the workflow projection (agent project, context --contract). There the auto-pin is a catalog entry, so its file is in inputRevisions and its reference in sources/sourceIds, which keeps the Amendment-1 invariant that every digest-moving input is listed. NOT a --workspace pack: it spans several bundles, which member's Constitution governs is undecided, and it is left byte-identical (design question raised to the dispatcher).

TESTS + MUTATIONS + GATES (LCLI-609). New test/agent-context-constitution.test.ts, 15 cases: AC1 'each profile's pack pins it first, whole, with catalog reason constitution' (alpha specialist pins+sources, beta sources-only, lead orchestrator); 'the profile's own pins follow it, in authored order, still with reason pinned'; 'plain: it renders under Pinned evidence ahead of the profile's pin, and in the catalog'; 'an unknown profile's degraded pack carries it too, and its warning says so'; 'the workflow projection pins it too, and names its file in inputRevisions and sources'; 'the --contract binding seam's sourceIds lead with it; without one they do not name it'; byte identity 'every output matches the digests measured on origin/dev e67b07af'. That case holds 26 LITERAL sha256 digests: plain+json stdout/stderr/exit for 3 profiles plus an unknown one, plus the projection with mtimeMs stripped. They were measured by extracting e67b07af's src/ (git archive) and running the same fixture twice (stable), so they are not derived from the code under test. Positive control 'the same fixture with a Constitution moves every pack's digest' (9 of 9 stdout digests move). AC2 'R12: a profile-declared Constitution is not auto-pinned' (with an in-test positive control); 'dedupe: an explicit whole-document pin is not duplicated, and keeps its authored place'; 'dedupe: a heading pin ...'; 'dedupe: a Constitution in the profile's ranked sources ...'. Budget: 'a Constitution the budget cannot hold fails exit 6, and the hint names it' (floor measured with and without, at-floor positive control); 'narrowing the Constitution to a heading in the profile lets the same budget compile'; 'a budget failure with no Constitution keeps the pre-LCLI-609 hint, word for word'. MUTATIONS, predicted in the file header before running. (1) R12 exclusion dropped (typeRuleFor: declared.types.has instead of isBuiltinTypeDeclaration): predicted exactly the R12 case; got 1 of 15 red, the R12 case. Full suite under that mutant: 5 red, 3813 pass (R12 here, the agents-governance R12 case, 2 Constitution and 1 Constants built-in-declaration cases in the type-rule tests). (2) Dedupe dropped (constitutionAutoPin ignores the profile's references): predicted the 3 dedupe cases plus the heading-narrowing budget case; got exactly those 4 of 15 red. Full suite under it: 4 red, 3814 pass, nothing outside this file. Both restored, with grep -c MUTANT = 0 in both files. REPO MEASUREMENT: this repo has no Constitution. For 4 packs (implementation, review, verification, no-such-profile) x plain/json x stdout/stderr, plus agent project implementation, the output of e67b07af's CLI and the output of the final CLI are IDENTICAL: 18 of 18 files, same docs tree. Positive control: a temporary docs/constitution.md (since removed) made all 9 stdout captures DIFFER, and implementation's catalog led with '- constitution (...; constitution)'. GATES on the final tree: bun test 3819 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 114 files; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); bun run typecheck exit 0; bunx biome check on the 6 changed TS files: 0 errors. Tools: bun 1.3.14, quest 0.10.0, lore from source (bun run src/cli.ts).

CHANGELOG (delegated to LCLI-599's release notes; CHANGELOG.md is owned by other open work and was not touched here). Sentence to use: '`lore agent context` now pins the bundle's built-in Constitution first in every pack, including every profile's pack, an unknown profile's degraded pack, and the pack `agent project` and `agent context --contract` embed. It carries catalog reason `constitution`, and in the projection its file is listed in `inputRevisions`. A profile that references the Constitution itself keeps its own reference and gets no second copy, a profile-declared `Constitution` type is never auto-pinned, and `--workspace` packs are unchanged. The auto-pin counts toward the budget like any pin, so a Constitution the budget cannot hold exits 6. With no built-in Constitution, every pack is byte-identical to before (LCLI-609; OPAG-425 R8 as clarified by Amendment 4).'

Precision on the mutant-1 full-suite note above: the three reds outside this task's files are in test/constitution.test.ts (2 cases, 'Constitution — rules attach only to lore's BUILT-IN declaration') and test/constants.test.ts (1 case, 'Constants — rules attach only to lore's BUILT-IN declaration'), not in a file named for type rules. AC evidence: AC1 and AC2 are checked on the 15-case file, the two mutants, and the 18-of-18 repo measurement with its positive control. AC3 is checked on the delegated CHANGELOG sentence above (LCLI-599 owns CHANGELOG.md) plus bun test 0 fail and bun run lore check exit 0.
